title: 8. In What Ways Does Your Protagonist Resist Change?
use_cases: Use when developing a protagonist's emotional arc and identifying their core obstacles
Implement when mapping out the second act of a screenplay to ensure consistent character struggle
Configure when defining the internal and external stakes to increase narrative tension
Use when identifying specific behaviors that demonstrate a character's fear of change
content:
Change hurts. The best scripts show characters fighting it every step, clinging to old habits, lashing out, or backsliding under stress.

Show your protagonist dodging hard truths. Maybe they rationalize, blame others, double down on bad habits, or freeze after a setback. Marlin’s overprotection in “Finding Nemo.” Carl’s refusal to move on in “Up.” Resistance is what makes victory feel earned.

List: Signs of Character Resistance

- Desperately defending flawed beliefs at any cost.
- Retreating to comfort zones when pressure spikes.
- Arguing with mentors or allies, pushing them away.
- Repeating failed behaviors even after negative results.

Don’t hand your protagonist an easy win. Layer setbacks and hesitation to build realism.

Real stakes grab attention. If failure costs nothing, readers stop caring. Define losses both internal and external—and ramp up the risk as your story unfolds.
